original: The clamour of New Winchester can be heard on the wind, familiar as a disagreeable uncle.
Lights in the distance. A stoker begins to sing a ballad about the chimneys of New Winchester.
Your final barrel of fuel. The sky still stretches before you.
You're down to the last of your fuel, now.
"That's our last barrel of fuel, captain," a crewman says. They try to keep their voice even.
Incognito Princess: "I see we're low on fuel. Understand that a great many things will burn before anything of mine does.'
Your fuel is desperately low, but the Signalman seems sanguine. He lights a cigarette and settles to watch the stars.
"Our fuel is low," remarks the Repentant Devil. He does not point fingers, but he does sound surprised and disappointed.
"Not to criticise," says the Inconvenient Aunt, "but do you expect us to get out and push?"
The Rat Brigade scour the train for unspent fuel. They find nothing of use.
Incautious Driver: "Uh-oh. Last of the fuel."
You've little food left, now. Soon, hunger will begin to bite.
You give the order for half rations, to eke out the last of your supplies.
You're down to the last dregs of your supplies. The unlabelled tins. The wormy biscuits.
A gloomy disquiet settles over your engine. Morale is fragile.
A growing unease. Patience erodes. Tempers fray.
A grim foreboding. What will become of you?
Nightmares prey upon your sleep. You manage without, for as long as you can.
A cold fear. Bleak prospects. Hope is fading.
A fatal pessimism grips the crew. They don't expect to see home again.
Dread settles on your locomotive, heavy and stifling as a deathbed blanket.
Without crew, you and your officers will struggle to manage.
The crew cabins are vacant. It's just you and your officers, now. An ominous quiet permeates your engine.
Your engine is a solemn, lonely place. Without crew, there are only the voices of you and your officers to break the silence.
Your Inadvisably Big Dog whines pitiably, afflicted by the dread that permeates your engine.
Your locomotive's morale is faltering. Even your Ratronaut thinks twice, now, before flinging himself into the velvet sky.
She tries to put a brave face on it, but even your Aunt is harrowed by the growing tension. You can smell the sherry on her breath.
Terror stalks your locomotive. The Princess sits in the unlit galley, her teeth white in the dark. "Invigorating, isn't it?" she whispers.
Fear grips your engine. The Rat Brigade have retreated to pipes and crannies, and bare sharp teeth at any who come near.
A mounting terror. The Driver's hands tremble on the wheel. "I thought I'd left fear behind," they say. "Apparently not."
Fatalistic Signalman: "Now I like a bit of peace and quiet, me. But a crew is widely considered to be a useful thing on a locomotive."
"Quiet, isn't it?" the Navigator notes, after passing the empty crew cabins.
Your mortal supplies are depleted. You have begun to eat petrichor, the food of the dead.
You have eaten the last of the mundane food. Only petrichor, the food of the dead, remains.
The last of your mortal provisions have been consumed. You must eat petrichor, now: pale as moonlight; sweet and brittle as spun sugar.
You have suffered a critical hit!
A well-placed hit shakes your locomotive.
A well-aimed shot penetrates your plating.
"No, you may not burn my librettos for fuel," the Clay Conductor says, after an imprudent suggestion by a stoker.
"We're low on fuel!" reports the Navigator. When a crewman looks over in alarm, he adds: "Only low. Not out. It's fine."
"We are low on fuel, Captain," the Forged Companion. "You should be aware: some of your stokers have tried to burn me."
The Eccentric confronts you about the condition of your engine. "She's starving, Captain. There's no fuel."
Incognito Princess: "Low supplies? I can tolerate only two courses at dinner, if I must."
The Repentant Devil is unconcerned by the lack of food. Does he even eat?
The Aunt snaps a ruler, briefly silencing the hungry crew. "Next to complain is first on the menu."
Supplies are low. The Rat Brigade has never looked more palatable.
The Incautious Driver is rueful. "Suppose we should have been cautious with the supplies. Next time."
"Please inform the crew that I am inedible," says the Forged Companion. "I would hate to cause indigestion."
"We're out of food," the Clay Conductor warns you. It's clear he expects you to resolve the problem.
The Navigator is embarrassed by a loud rumble from his stomach. "It's not a criticism, Captain. I promise!"
A crewman hurries by, bleeding. However low supplies are, he won't try to eat the Eccentric's cats again.
Fear prevails. The Forged Companion's poetry grows increasingly disjointed and hallucinatory.
"I like the quiet," the Clay Conductor rumbles. "But even were I willing, I can't perform the work of an entire crew."
"The fuel is low," says the Chiropterous Hoarder. "Fortunately, some of us have wings." It sounds gently smug.
The Chiropterous Hoarder will not come out of the walls and a low, hungry chittering rattles through every pipe.
"I look after your biscuits and your sherry and your salt," says the Hoarder. "The crew was your problem."
"Tally ho!" Your Aunt whoops as your engine thunders.
The Rat Brigade form a ratty chain to anchor each other as your locomotive leaps forward.
The Driver's expression is unholy as you order full steam. "That's the ticket!"
The Devil quirks an eyebrow as your locomotive rockets across the sky. "Are you trying to impress me, Captain?"
The Princess: "Can't this thing go any faster, capta—aaaAAA not like that!"
Chaos in the galley as the Eccentric's cats bounce off the walls, to the consternation of the crew.
The Fortunate Navigator laughs as your locomotive leaps eagerly forward.
The Stalwart Navigator smiles and leans back in his seat as the engine roars.
The Vagabond plays a jig on his harmonica, using the breakneck rattle of your engine as percussion.
"Hubris!" the Signalman shouts over the noise of the engine. "No man can live at this speed!"
As the engine reaches full steam, the Conductor claps his hands with glee. Then he pretends it never happened.
Dilly is terrified by your sudden speed. She makes a noise like a balloon being hugged, then scurries away.
Your dog enjoys your breakneck speed. He leans from an open window, tongue flapping.
As the acceleration kicks in, your Useless Cat gives you a filthy look and sinks its claws into your lap.
Your pangolin curls into a ball. It refuses to come out until you return to a more sensible speed.
Your locomotive lurches forward. Your Obviously Delicious Rabbit tumbles into a simmering pot of soup. A stoker rescues it.
Ahead, the sky is full of midnight.
"We have to turn back, captain. Ahead lie the wastes."
Before you stretches a starless waste, hounded by the wind.
You are near the edge of this district of the sky. Little lies beyond, except a cold death.
The skies ahead are vacant and dead.
Turn back. You are at the edge of the living sky.
Light washes over you. You are in the heart of a star's power.
